titulo: Tuning giant surface potential in OLEDs can improve efficiency and lifespan
resumo: Organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) power many display screens, but their efficiency can be limited by energy lost inside the device. As organic layers are deposited, their molecules can align to create an internal electrical potential known as giant surface potential (GSP). When this potential draws excess positive charges, or holes, near the light-emitting layer, they can interfere with light-producing excitons. This process, called exciton–polaron quenching, reduces emitted light and can affect device performance.

titulo: NSF’s X-Labs Program Draws Support From Charities and Investors
resumo: When the U.S. National Science Foundation began its X-Labs program in May, the agency said the higher-risk, higher-funded awards would create new kinds of partnerships that would confront urgent scientific and technological challenges. Now, the NSF is doubling down on the idea, with an announcement in October that charities, companies, and investment funds would provide X-Lab winners practical support such as laboratory space, software, shared equipment, and access to key data and expert guidance. The help provided by these organizations, which the NSF is calling “ consortium partners ,” will not give them ownership stakes in the X-Labs projects. The addition of the consortium partners may help the initial winners—who will be announced later in November or December and who receive US $1.5 million for a 9-month planning phase—reach the aggressive targets needed to compete for much larger $50 million multi-year grants. “It’s a way of telling X-Labs applicants you don’t need to reinvent the wheel, so you’re not spending half of your X-Labs money to go build or buy basic infrastructure,” says Matt Cimaglia , an investor in consortium partners Occam Foundry and Florida Quantum Center .

titulo: With Zen 6, AMD’s next great gaming CPU could have it all
resumo: AMD’s best gaming CPUs have eight cores. Its next generation could pack twelve into the same kind of chiplet, making every single one of them faster. AMD’s Zen 6 architecture puts 12 full-performance cores and 48MB of shared L3 cache on a single chiplet, up from eight cores and 32MB with Zen 5. That’s a 50 percent jump in both, and AMD is rebuilding the cores themselves to squeeze more performance out of every clock cycle. The company revealed the finer details during a technical deep-dive into its next-generation Epyc “Venice” server processors. The next generation of Ryzen processors hasn’t been announced yet, but both families share the same underlying Zen 6 architecture. And for gamers, the implications go well beyond stuffing more cores onto a spec sheet, though that’s obviously fantastic. Twelve cores, one chiplet A core complex die (CCD) is a group of CPU cores sharing a pool of fast L3 cache, which keeps frequently used data close instead of forcing trips to slower system memory. Today’s 12-core Ryzen processors need two CCDs because Zen 5 fits only eight cores into each one. That works, but communicating between separate chiplets takes longer than communicating within one.

titulo: [$] Additional hardening for the glibc dynamic linker
resumo: The Node.js project recently had a security vulnerability that affected its Brotli decoder. The bug was a buffer overflow , but the particular way that official Node.js binaries are built for Linux meant that one of the main protections against turning a buffer overflow into remote code execution, address space layout randomization (ASLR) could not be turned on. If ASLR had been enabled, the bug would still be exploitable in theory, but much more difficult to exploit in practice. In response, the GNU C Library (glibc) is considering a new set of tunable settings to allow administrators to forbid programs that do not support ASLR. The new settings, while a welcome hardening measure, may not address the root problem.

titulo: Windows 11 might be getting a central hub for app updates
resumo: Most Windows programs use their own systems to check for and install updates. However, this can result in an annoying number of reminders. It also carries the risk of missing important security updates. Windows Latest discovered that a new page for program updates has appeared under Settings > Apps in a preview version of Windows 11 26H2. The feature is based on the Windows Update Orchestration Platform (UOP), a technology Microsoft unveiled in 2025 that enables software developers to connect their existing update systems to Windows. The idea is that Windows will automatically check for available updates and schedule installations at suitable times. Among other things, the system can take into account whether the computer is in use, the battery level, and the network connection. Support is intended to cover traditional Windows programs installed outside the Microsoft Store, though this requires developers to connect their software to the system themselves. The new page is not yet fully functional, and it remains unclear when the feature will become available to all Windows 11 users.

titulo: AMD confirms bug causing excessive SSD wear
resumo: If you’ve noticed your SSD filling up or experiencing heavy background activity lately, an ongoing bug in AMD’s software might be to blame. The fault lies within AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition. It has been reported by several users, according to Tom’s Hardware . The underlying cause appears to be the AMD External Events Utility service, which, on some computers, continuously writes data to the system drive. Users have reported write speeds of between 0.3 and 5 MB/s. In the worst reported case, this equates to over 400 GB per day. One user states that the storage device’s reported health status has deteriorated by around one percent a month over a period of 16 months, though this has not been verified. The issue has been reported in both Windows 10 and Windows 11 and appears across several versions of AMD’s drivers, though not all users are affected. AMD has confirmed the bug and states that a fix is expected in driver version 26.11.1, which does not yet have a confirmed release date.
